artifact_status: Textured motion review of the requested full arrival order; silent and not game-integrated.
method: Played the full encoded 28-second cut at 1x in the in-app browser, inspected sampled playback frames and sought decoded entry frames at 4.10, 6.00 and 7.95 seconds. Also inspected native space start/mid/end and entry start/mid/end previews. This is sampled visual inspection plus full playback completion, not a claim of watching every individual frame.
counter_limits: Browser presentation/decode counters have different baselines. FFprobe separately confirms all 672 encoded frames.
findings: Second Wind travels bow-first toward the planet at a restrained fixed aspect; damage and component identity match the retained landing hull.
The orbital view establishes green land, seas, broken cloud and a large storm while keeping the vessel much smaller than the planet.
Warm exterior filaments fade into pale clouds inside the same sealed-window framing. The cabin remains readable and its retained material does not receive new simulated glow lighting.
The decoded 7.95-second frame shows the accepted forest and Atlas composition. The source entry endpoint is pixel-identical to forest output zero, with a single shared 1/24-second boundary sample.
The requested order is complete: space, entry, forest, fields, port, damaged landing. Changes in altitude and scale are editorial time ellipses.
The cut ends on the previously reviewed damaged landing and simpler dock finish.
limits: Four-second opening excerpts establish timing and continuity; final pacing remains dependent on eventual narration and sound.
Planet is a fixed distant scenery plate; moving ship is real retained geometry with bounded projected surface coverage.
Entry uses authored layered effects and a retained daylight cabin finish, not plasma, aerodynamic or lighting simulation.
No new narration, audio mix, campaign trigger, skip behavior or runtime integration is included.
First entry render has after-render scene/frame hashes only; its report explicitly does not claim an in-process before/after hash binding. Future renders implement that instrumentation.
Fine motion artifacts outside inspected samples and final creative acceptance remain for user review.
